page: Microsoft Azure DC4es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon TDX processor operating at 4.2 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache alongside support for modern vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic instruction sets such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The server does not bundle local disk storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external storage attachments.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core performance, led by a Geekbench single-core score of 1949.0, placing it in the upper quartile due to its 4.2 GHz clock speed and updated core architecture. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput is restricted by the 2-core, 4-thread execution envelope, resulting in lower-tier results in multi-core stress-ng (3933.18) and Geekbench multi-core (4364.0), as well as software compilation tests. Mixed workloads such as text processing, image processing, and PassMark database operations land in the mid-range performance tier. Redis SET throughput registers at 5.19 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, DC4es_v6 delivers solid per-thread performance and advanced instruction acceleration, though overall throughput is inherently limited by core density. Because local storage is absent, overall operational overhead must account for network-attached storage dependencies. This hardware profile is best matched with entry to mid-tier general-purpose enterprise applications, containerized microservices, light caching layers, and database workloads that rely more on single-thread frequency and memory consistency than wide parallel scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure DC4es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V, equipped with a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon TDX processor featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores. It provides 16.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache and support for AVX-512, AMX, and hardware cryptography instructions. The instance includes no integrated local storage or discrete GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark measurements demonstrate strong single-core performance in Geekbench, offset by lower multi-threaded throughput due to the four-vCPU limit in high-concurrency tasks. Memory performance and database operations consistently fall into median brackets. The DC4es_v6 is suitable for general application hosting, lightweight database workloads, microservices, and intermediate compute tasks requiring modern instruction sets.
